notes: The italicized *came down* of the Ephraim colon is given to the written יָרְדוּ of the Machir colon under rule 34's carve-out — the Hebrew writes the verb once in the coordination and the ASV realizes it twice, so both occurrences are one discontinuous unit headed on the first. Marking it `added` under rule 34's supplied-lexical-verb clause was the competing reading.
The suffix of שָׁרְשָׁם is realized by *they whose*, the supplied antecedent and the relative together (rule 18), headed on *they*; heading on *whose* was the competing reading.

The בְּ of בְּשֵׁבֶט is `unrepresented`, its object promoted to the direct object of *handle* (rule 40); the supplied determiner of the recast possessive *the marshal's staff* goes to the possessor's word (rule 29).
